parts.antiphonLat: Convértere, * Dómine, et éripe ánimam meam: quóniam non est in morte, qui memor sit tui.
parts.antiphonEng: Return, O Lord, deliver my soul * O save me for thy mercy's sake.

verses.lat: Dómine, ne in furóre tuo árguas me, * neque in ira tua corrípias me.
verses.eng: Lord, rebuke me not in thy indignation, * nor chastise me in thy wrath.

verses.lat: Miserére mei, Dómine, quóniam infírmus sum: * sana me, Dómine, quóniam conturbáta sunt ossa mea.
verses.eng: Have mercy on me, O Lord, for I am weak: * heal me, O Lord, for my bones are troubled.

verses.lat: Et ánima mea turbáta est valde: * sed tu, Dómine, úsquequo?
verses.eng: And my soul is troubled exceedingly: * but thou, O Lord, how long?

verses.lat: Convértere, Dómine, et éripe ánimam meam: * salvum me fac propter misericórdiam tuam.
verses.eng: Turn to me, O Lord, and deliver my soul: * O save me for thy mercy’s sake.

verses.lat: Quóniam non est in morte qui memor sit tui: * in inférno autem quis confitébitur tibi?
verses.eng: For there is no one in death, that is mindful of thee: * and who shall confess to thee in hell?

verses.lat: Laborávi in gémitu meo, † lavábo per síngulas noctes lectum meum: * lácrimis meis stratum meum rigábo.
verses.eng: I have laboured in my groanings, † every night I will wash my bed: * I will water my couch with my tears.

verses.lat: Turbátus est a furóre óculus meus: * inveterávi inter omnes inimícos meos.
verses.eng: My eye is troubled through indignation: * I have grown old amongst all my enemies.

verses.lat: Discédite a me, omnes, qui operámini iniquitátem: * quóniam exaudívit Dóminus vocem fletus mei.
verses.eng: Depart from me, all ye workers of iniquity: * for the Lord hath heard the voice of my weeping.

verses.lat: Exaudívit Dóminus deprecatiónem meam, * Dóminus oratiónem meam suscépit.
verses.eng: The Lord hath heard my supplication: * the Lord hath received my prayer.

verses.lat: Erubéscant, et conturbéntur veheménter omnes inimíci mei: * convertántur et erubéscant valde velóciter.
verses.eng: Let all my enemies be ashamed, and be very much troubled: * let them be turned back, and be ashamed very speedily.

verses.lat: Réquiem ætérnam * dona eis, Dómine.
verses.eng: Eternal rest * grant unto them, O Lord.

verses.lat: Et lux perpétua * lúceat eis.
verses.eng: And let perpetual light * shine upon them.

parts.rubric: Recited in full according to the Vulgate psalter; concluded with Réquiem ætérnam dona eis, Dómine: et lux perpétua lúceat eis, in place of Glória Patri.

parts.label: Psalmus 7
parts.antiphonLat: Nequándo rápiat * ut leo ánimam meam, dum non est qui rédimat, neque qui salvum fáciat.
parts.antiphonEng: Lest he tear my soul like a lion, * while there is none to deliver, or to save.

verses.lat: Dómine, Deus meus, in te sperávi: * salvum me fac ex ómnibus persequéntibus me, et líbera me.
verses.eng: O Lord my God, in thee have I put my trust: * save me from all them that persecute me, and deliver me.

verses.lat: Nequándo rápiat ut leo ánimam meam, * dum non est qui rédimat, neque qui salvum fáciat.
verses.eng: Lest at any time he seize upon my soul like a lion, * while there is no one to redeem me, nor to save.

verses.lat: Dómine, Deus meus, si feci istud, * si est iníquitas in mánibus meis:
verses.eng: O Lord my God, if I have done this thing, * if there be iniquity in my hands:

verses.lat: Si réddidi retribuéntibus mihi mala, * décidam mérito ab inimícis meis inánis.
verses.eng: If I have rendered to them that repaid me evils, * let me deservedly fall empty before my enemies.

verses.lat: Persequátur inimícus ánimam meam, † et comprehéndat, et concúlcet in terra vitam meam, * et glóriam meam in púlverem dedúcat.
verses.eng: Let the enemy pursue my soul, † and take it, and tread down my life on the earth, * and bring down my glory to the dust.

verses.lat: Exsúrge, Dómine, in ira tua: * et exaltáre in fínibus inimicórum meórum.
verses.eng: Rise up, O Lord, in thy anger: * and be thou exalted in the borders of my enemies.

verses.lat: Et exsúrge, Dómine, Deus meus, in præcépto quod mandásti: * (8a) et synagóga populórum circúmdabit te.
verses.eng: And arise, O Lord my God, in the precept which thou hast commanded: * (8a) and a congregation of people shall surround thee.

verses.lat: Et propter hanc in altum regrédere: * (9a) Dóminus júdicat pópulos.
verses.eng: And for their sakes return thou on high. * (9a) The Lord judgeth the people.

verses.lat: Júdica me, Dómine, secúndum justítiam meam, * et secúndum innocéntiam meam super me.
verses.eng: Judge me, O Lord, according to my justice, * and according to my innocence in me.

verses.lat: Consumétur nequítia peccatórum, et díriges justum, * scrutans corda et renes, Deus.
verses.eng: The wickedness of sinners shall be brought to nought: and thou shalt direct the just: * the searcher of hearts and reins is God.

verses.lat: Justum adjutórium meum a Dómino, * qui salvos facit rectos corde.
verses.eng: Just is my help from the Lord: * who saveth the upright of heart.

verses.lat: Deus judex justus, fortis, et pátiens: * numquid iráscitur per síngulos dies?
verses.eng: God is a just judge, strong and patient: * is he angry every day?

verses.lat: Nisi convérsi fuéritis, gládium suum vibrábit: * arcum suum teténdit, et parávit illum.
verses.eng: Except you will be converted, he will brandish his sword: * he hath bent his bow, and made it ready.

verses.lat: Et in eo parávit vasa mortis: * sagíttas suas ardéntibus effécit.
verses.eng: And in it he hath prepared the instruments of death, * he hath made ready his arrows for them that burn.

verses.lat: Ecce, partúriit injustítiam: * concépit dolórem, et péperit iniquitátem.
verses.eng: Behold he hath been in labour with injustice; * he hath conceived sorrow, and brought forth iniquity.

verses.lat: Lacum apéruit, et effódit eum: * et íncidit in fóveam quam fecit.
verses.eng: He hath opened a pit and dug it: * and he is fallen into the hole he made.

verses.lat: Convertétur dolor ejus in caput ejus: * et in vérticem ipsíus iníquitas ejus descéndet.
verses.eng: His sorrow shall be turned on his own head: * and his iniquity shall come down upon his crown.

verses.lat: Confitébor Dómino secúndum justítiam ejus: * et psallam nómini Dómini altíssimi.
verses.eng: I will give glory to the Lord according to his justice: * and will sing to the name of the Lord the most High.

verses.lat: Réquiem ætérnam * dona eis, Dómine.
verses.eng: Eternal rest * grant unto them, O Lord.

verses.lat: Et lux perpétua * lúceat eis.
verses.eng: And let perpetual light * shine upon them.

parts.rubric: Recited in full according to the Vulgate psalter; concluded with Réquiem ætérnam dona eis, Dómine: et lux perpétua lúceat eis, in place of Glória Patri.

parts.label: Versicle after Nocturn I
parts.lat: ℣. A porta ínferi.
parts.eng: ℣. From the gates of hell.

parts.label: Pater Noster (silently)
parts.lat: Pater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum. Advéniat regnum tuum. Fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum quotidiánum da nobis hódie, et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris. Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem, sed líbera nos a malo. Amen.
parts.eng: Our Father, who art in heaven, hallowed be Thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth, as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread, and forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us. And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil. Amen.
parts.rubric: Said silently.

parts.label: Léctio I
parts.lat: Parce mihi, Dómine; nihil enim sunt dies mei. Quid est homo, quia magníficas eum? aut quid appónis erga eum cor tuum? Vísitas eum dilúculo, et súbito probas illum. Usquequo non parcis mihi, nec dimíttis me, ut glútiam salívam meam? Peccávi, quid fáciam tibi, o custos hóminum? quare posuísti me contrárium tibi, et factus sum mihimetípsi gravis? Cur non tollis peccátum meum, et quare non aufers iniquitátem meam? Ecce nunc in púlvere dórmiam: et, si mane me quæsíeris, non subsístam.
parts.eng: Spare me, for my days are nothing. What is a man that thou shouldst magnify him? or why dost thou set thy heart upon him? Thou visitest him early in the morning, and thou provest him suddenly. How long wilt thou not spare me, nor suffer me to swallow down my spittle? I have sinned: what shall I do to thee, O keeper of men? why hast thou set me opposite to thee, and I am become burdensome to myself? Why dost thou not remove my sin, and why dost thou not take away my iniquity? Behold now I shall sleep in the dust: and if thou seek me in the morning, I shall not be.

parts.label: Tu autem
parts.lat: Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
parts.eng: But Thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

parts.label: Responsórium I
parts.v1Lat:
℟. Credo quod Redémptor meus vivit, et in novíssimo die de terra surrectúrus sum,
* Et in carne mea vidébo Deum Salvatórem meum.
parts.v1Eng:
℟. I believe that my Redeemer liveth, and that I shall stand up from the earth at the latter day,
* And in my flesh shall I see God my Saviour.
parts.r1Lat: ℣. Quem visúrus sum ego ipse, et non álius; et óculi mei conspectúri sunt.
parts.r1Eng: ℣. Whom I shall see for myself, and mine eyes shall behold, and not another.
parts.r2Lat: ℟. Et in carne mea vidébo Deum Salvatórem meum.
parts.r2Eng: ℟. And in my flesh shall I see God my Saviour.

parts.label: Léctio II
parts.lat: Tædet ánimam meam vitæ meæ; dimíttam advérsum me elóquium meum: loquar in amaritúdine ánimæ meæ. Dicam Deo: Noli me condemnáre; índica mihi cur me ita júdices. Numquid bonum tibi vidétur, si calumniéris me, et ópprimas me opus mánuum tuárum, et consílium impiórum ádjuves? Numquid óculi cárnei tibi sunt? aut sicut videt homo, et tu vidébis? Numquid sicut dies hóminis dies tui, et anni tui sicut humána sunt témpora, ut quæras iniquitátem meam, et peccátum meum scrutéris, et scias quia nihil ímpium fécerim, cum sit nemo qui de manu tua possit erúere?
parts.eng: My soul is weary of my life, I will let go my speech against myself, I will speak in the bitterness of my soul. I will say to God: Do not condemn me: tell me why thou judgest me so. Doth it seem good to thee that thou shouldst calumniate me, and oppress me, the work of thy own hands, and help the counsel of the wicked? Hast thou eyes of flesh: or, shalt thou see as man seeth? Are thy days as the days of man, and are thy years as the times of men: That thou shouldst inquire after my iniquity, and search after my sin? And shouldst know that I have done no wicked thing, whereas there is no man that can deliver out of thy hand.

parts.label: Tu autem
parts.lat: Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
parts.eng: But Thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

parts.label: Responsórium II
parts.v1Lat:
℟. Qui Lázarum resuscitásti a monuménto fœ́tidum,
* Tu eis, Dómine, dona réquiem, et locum indulgéntiæ.
parts.v1Eng:
℟. Thou Who didst call up Lazarus from the grave after that he had begun to stink,
* Do Thou, O Lord, grant them rest and a place of forgiveness.
parts.r1Lat: ℣. Qui ventúrus es judicáre vivos et mórtuos, et sǽculum per ignem.
parts.r1Eng: ℣. Thou Who shalt come to judge the quick and dead, and the world by fire.
parts.r2Lat: ℟. Tu eis, Dómine, dona réquiem, et locum indulgéntiæ.
parts.r2Eng: ℟. Do Thou, O Lord, grant them rest and a place of forgiveness.

parts.label: Léctio III
parts.lat: Manus tuæ fecérunt me, et plasmavérunt me totum in circúitu: et sic repénte præcípitas me? Meménto, quæso, quod sicut lutum féceris me, et in púlverem redúces me. Nonne sicut lac mulsísti me, et sicut cáseum me coagulásti? Pelle et cárnibus vestísti me; óssibus et nervis compegísti me. Vitam et misericórdiam tribuísti mihi, et visitátio tua custodívit spíritum meum.
parts.eng: Thy hands have made me, and fashioned me wholly round about, and dost thou thus cast me down headlong on a sudden? Remember, I beseech thee, that thou hast made me as the clay, and thou wilt bring me into dust again. Hast thou not milked me as milk, and curdled me like cheese? Thou hast clothed me with skin and flesh: thou hast put me together with bones and sinews: Thou hast granted me life and mercy, and thy visitation hath preserved my spirit.

parts.label: Tu autem
parts.lat: Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
parts.eng: But Thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

parts.label: Responsórium III
parts.v1Lat:
℟. Dómine, quando véneris judicáre terram, ubi me abscóndam a vultu iræ tuæ?
* Quia peccávi nimis in vita mea.
parts.v1Eng:
℟. Lord, when Thou comest to judge the earth, where shall I hide myself from the face of thy wrath?
* For I have sinned greatly in my life.
parts.r1Lat: ℣. Commíssa mea pavésco, et ante te erubésco: dum véneris judicáre, noli me condemnáre.
parts.r1Eng: ℣. I dread my sins, I blush before thee I see the great tribunal set! In fear and terror I implore thee, Forgive when soul and Judge are met!
parts.r2Lat:
℟. Quia peccávi nimis in vita mea.
℣. Réquiem ætérnam dona eis, Dómine: et lux perpétua lúceat eis.
℟. Quia peccávi nimis in vita mea.
parts.r2Eng:
℟. For I have sinned greatly in my life.
℣. Eternal rest grant unto them, O Lord, and let perpetual light shine upon them.
℟. For I have sinned greatly in my life.

parts.label: Psalmus 22
parts.antiphonLat: In loco páscuæ * ibi me collocávit.
parts.antiphonEng: He maketh me to lie down * in green pastures.

verses.lat: Dóminus regit me, et nihil mihi déerit: * in loco páscuæ ibi me collocávit.
verses.eng: The Lord ruleth me: and I shall want nothing. * He hath set me in a place of pasture.

verses.lat: Super aquam refectiónis educávit me: * ánimam meam convértit.
verses.eng: He hath brought me up, on the water of refreshment: * he hath converted my soul.

verses.lat: Dedúxit me super sémitas justítiæ, * propter nomen suum.
verses.eng: He hath led me on the paths of justice, * for his own name’s sake.

verses.lat: Nam, et si ambulávero in médio umbræ mortis, non timébo mala: * quóniam tu mecum es.
verses.eng: For though I should walk in the midst of the shadow of death, I will fear no evils, * for thou art with me.

verses.lat: Virga tua, et báculus tuus: * ipsa me consoláta sunt.
verses.eng: Thy rod and thy staff, * they have comforted me.

verses.lat: Parásti in conspéctu meo mensam, * advérsus eos, qui tríbulant me.
verses.eng: Thou hast prepared a table before me * against them that afflict me.

verses.lat: Impinguásti in óleo caput meum: * et calix meus inébrians quam præclárus est!
verses.eng: Thou hast anointed my head with oil; * and my chalice which inebriateth me, how goodly is it!

verses.lat: Et misericórdia tua subsequétur me * ómnibus diébus vitæ meæ:
verses.eng: And thy mercy will follow me * all the days of my life.

verses.lat: Et ut inhábitem in domo Dómini, * in longitúdinem diérum.
verses.eng: And that I may dwell in the house of the Lord * unto length of days.

verses.lat: Réquiem ætérnam * dona eis, Dómine.
verses.eng: Eternal rest * grant unto them, O Lord.

verses.lat: Et lux perpétua * lúceat eis.
verses.eng: And let perpetual light * shine upon them.

parts.rubric: Recited in full according to the Vulgate psalter; concluded with Réquiem ætérnam dona eis, Dómine: et lux perpétua lúceat eis, in place of Glória Patri.

parts.label: Psalmus 24
parts.antiphonLat: Delícta * juventútis meæ, et ignorántias meas ne memíneris, Dómine.
parts.antiphonEng: Lord, remember not the sins of my youth, * nor my transgressions.

verses.lat: Ad te, Dómine, levávi ánimam meam: * Deus meus, in te confído, non erubéscam.
verses.eng: To thee, O Lord, have I lifted up my soul: * In thee, O my God, I put my trust; let me not be ashamed.

verses.lat: Neque irrídeant me inimíci mei: * étenim univérsi, qui sústinent te, non confundéntur.
verses.eng: Neither let my enemies laugh at me: * for none of them that wait on thee shall be confounded.

verses.lat: Confundántur omnes iníqua agéntes * supervácue.
verses.eng: Let all them be confounded that act unjust things * without cause.

verses.lat: Vias tuas, Dómine, demónstra mihi: * et sémitas tuas édoce me.
verses.eng: Shew, O Lord, thy ways to me, * and teach me thy paths.

verses.lat: Dírige me in veritáte tua, et doce me: * quia tu es, Deus, salvátor meus, et te sustínui tota die.
verses.eng: Direct me in thy truth, and teach me; * for thou art God my Saviour; and on thee have I waited all the day long.

verses.lat: Reminíscere miseratiónum tuárum, Dómine, * et misericordiárum tuárum, quæ a sǽculo sunt.
verses.eng: Remember, O Lord, thy bowels of compassion; * and thy mercies that are from the beginning of the world.

verses.lat: Delícta juventútis meæ, * et ignorántias meas ne memíneris.
verses.eng: The sins of my youth * and my ignorances do not remember.

verses.lat: Secúndum misericórdiam tuam meménto mei tu: * propter bonitátem tuam, Dómine.
verses.eng: According to thy mercy remember thou me: * for thy goodness’ sake, O Lord.

verses.lat: Dulcis et rectus Dóminus: * propter hoc legem dabit delinquéntibus in via.
verses.eng: The Lord is sweet and righteous: * therefore he will give a law to sinners in the way.

verses.lat: Díriget mansuétos in judício: * docébit mites vias suas.
verses.eng: He will guide the mild in judgment: * he will teach the meek his ways.

verses.lat: Univérsæ viæ Dómini, misericórdia et véritas, * requiréntibus testaméntum ejus et testimónia ejus.
verses.eng: All the ways of the Lord are mercy and truth, * to them that seek after his covenant and his testimonies.

verses.lat: Propter nomen tuum, Dómine, propitiáberis peccáto meo: * multum est enim.
verses.eng: For thy name’s sake, O Lord, thou wilt pardon my sin: * for it is great.

verses.lat: Quis est homo qui timet Dóminum? * legem státuit ei in via, quam elégit.
verses.eng: Who is the man that feareth the Lord? * He hath appointed him a law in the way he hath chosen.

verses.lat: Ánima ejus in bonis demorábitur: * et semen ejus hereditábit terram.
verses.eng: His soul shall dwell in good things: * and his seed shall inherit the land.

verses.lat: Firmaméntum est Dóminus timéntibus eum: * et testaméntum ipsíus ut manifestétur illis.
verses.eng: The Lord is a firmament to them that fear him: * and his covenant shall be made manifest to them.

verses.lat: Óculi mei semper ad Dóminum: * quóniam ipse evéllet de láqueo pedes meos.
verses.eng: My eyes are ever towards the Lord: * for he shall pluck my feet out of the snare.

verses.lat: Réspice in me, et miserére mei: * quia únicus et pauper sum ego.
verses.eng: Look thou upon me, and have mercy on me; * for I am alone and poor.

verses.lat: Tribulatiónes cordis mei multiplicátæ sunt: * de necessitátibus meis érue me.
verses.eng: The troubles of my heart are multiplied: * deliver me from my necessities.

verses.lat: Vide humilitátem meam, et labórem meum: * et dimítte univérsa delícta mea.
verses.eng: See my abjection and my labour; * and forgive me all my sins.

verses.lat: Réspice inimícos meos quóniam multiplicáti sunt, * et ódio iníquo odérunt me.
verses.eng: Consider my enemies for they are multiplied, * and have hated me with an unjust hatred.

verses.lat: Custódi ánimam meam, et érue me: * non erubéscam quóniam sperávi in te.
verses.eng: Keep thou my soul, and deliver me: * I shall not be ashamed, for I have hoped in thee.

verses.lat: Innocéntes et recti adhæsérunt mihi: * quia sustínui te.
verses.eng: The innocent and the upright have adhered to me: * because I have waited on thee.

verses.lat: Líbera, Deus, Israël, * ex ómnibus tribulatiónibus suis.
verses.eng: Deliver Israel, O God, * from all his tribulations.

verses.lat: Réquiem ætérnam * dona eis, Dómine.
verses.eng: Eternal rest * grant unto them, O Lord.

verses.lat: Et lux perpétua * lúceat eis.
verses.eng: And let perpetual light * shine upon them.

parts.rubric: Recited in full according to the Vulgate psalter; concluded with Réquiem ætérnam dona eis, Dómine: et lux perpétua lúceat eis, in place of Glória Patri.

parts.label: Psalmus 26
parts.antiphonLat: Credo vidére * bona Dómini in terra vivéntium.
parts.antiphonEng: I believe that I shall yet see the goodness of the Lord * in the land of the living.

verses.lat: Dóminus illuminátio mea, et salus mea, * quem timébo?
verses.eng: The Lord is my light and my salvation, * whom shall I fear?

verses.lat: Dóminus protéctor vitæ meæ, * a quo trepidábo?
verses.eng: The Lord is the protector of my life: * of whom shall I be afraid?

verses.lat: Dum apprópiant super me nocéntes, * ut edant carnes meas:
verses.eng: Whilst the wicked draw near against me, * to eat my flesh.

verses.lat: Qui tríbulant me inimíci mei, * ipsi infirmáti sunt, et cecidérunt.
verses.eng: My enemies that trouble me, * have themselves been weakened, and have fallen.

verses.lat: Si consístant advérsum me castra, * non timébit cor meum.
verses.eng: If armies in camp should stand together against me, * my heart shall not fear.

verses.lat: Si exsúrgat advérsum me prǽlium, * in hoc ego sperábo.
verses.eng: If a battle should rise up against me, * in this will I be confident.

verses.lat: Unam pétii a Dómino, hanc requíram, * ut inhábitem in domo Dómini ómnibus diébus vitæ meæ:
verses.eng: One thing I have asked of the Lord, this will I seek after; * that I may dwell in the house of the Lord all the days of my life.

verses.lat: Ut vídeam voluptátem Dómini, * et vísitem templum ejus.
verses.eng: That I may see the delight of the Lord, * and may visit his temple.

verses.lat: Quóniam abscóndit me in tabernáculo suo: * in die malórum protéxit me in abscóndito tabernáculi sui.
verses.eng: For he hath hidden me in his tabernacle; * in the day of evils, he hath protected me in the secret place of his tabernacle.

verses.lat: In petra exaltávit me: * et nunc exaltávit caput meum super inimícos meos.
verses.eng: He hath exalted me upon a rock: * and now he hath lifted up my head above my enemies.

verses.lat: Circuívi, et immolávi in tabernáculo ejus hóstiam vociferatiónis: * cantábo, et psalmum dicam Dómino.
verses.eng: I have gone round, and have offered up in his tabernacle a sacrifice of jubilation: * I will sing, and recite a psalm to the Lord.

verses.lat: Exáudi, Dómine, vocem meam, qua clamávi ad te: * miserére mei, et exáudi me.
verses.eng: Hear, O Lord, my voice, with which I have cried to thee: * have mercy on me and hear me.

verses.lat: Tibi dixit cor meum, exquisívit te fácies mea: * fáciem tuam, Dómine, requíram.
verses.eng: My heart hath said to thee: My face hath sought thee: * thy face, O Lord, will I still seek.

verses.lat: Ne avértas fáciem tuam a me: * ne declínes in ira a servo tuo.
verses.eng: Turn not away thy face from me; * decline not in thy wrath from thy servant.

verses.lat: Adjútor meus esto: * ne derelínquas me, neque despícias me, Deus, salutáris meus.
verses.eng: Be thou my helper, * forsake me not; do not thou despise me, O God my Saviour.

verses.lat: Quóniam pater meus, et mater mea dereliquérunt me: * Dóminus autem assúmpsit me.
verses.eng: For my father and my mother have left me: * but the Lord hath taken me up.

verses.lat: Legem pone mihi, Dómine, in via tua: * et dírige me in sémitam rectam propter inimícos meos.
verses.eng: Set me, O Lord, a law in thy way, * and guide me in the right path, because of my enemies.

verses.lat: Ne tradíderis me in ánimas tribulántium me: * quóniam insurrexérunt in me testes iníqui, et mentíta est iníquitas sibi.
verses.eng: Deliver me not over to the will of them that trouble me; * for unjust witnesses have risen up against me; and iniquity hath lied to itself.

verses.lat: Credo vidére bona Dómini * in terra vivéntium.
verses.eng: I believe to see the good things of the Lord * in the land of the living.

verses.lat: Exspécta Dóminum, viríliter age: * et confortétur cor tuum, et sústine Dóminum.
verses.eng: Expect the Lord, do manfully, * and let thy heart take courage, and wait thou for the Lord.

verses.lat: Réquiem ætérnam * dona eis, Dómine.
verses.eng: Eternal rest * grant unto them, O Lord.

verses.lat: Et lux perpétua * lúceat eis.
verses.eng: And let perpetual light * shine upon them.

parts.rubric: Recited in full according to the Vulgate psalter; concluded with Réquiem ætérnam dona eis, Dómine: et lux perpétua lúceat eis, in place of Glória Patri.

parts.label: Versicle after Nocturn II
parts.lat: ℣. Cóllocet eos Dóminus cum princípibus.
parts.eng: ℣. May the Lord set them with princes;
parts.engR: ℟. Even with the princes of his people.

parts.label: Pater Noster (silently)
parts.lat: Pater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum. Advéniat regnum tuum. Fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum quotidiánum da nobis hódie, et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris. Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem, sed líbera nos a malo. Amen.
parts.eng: Our Father, who art in heaven, hallowed be Thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth, as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread, and forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us. And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil. Amen.
parts.rubric: Said silently.

parts.label: Léctio IV
parts.lat: Respónde mihi. Quantas hábeo iniquitátes et peccáta? scélera mea et delícta osténde mihi. Cur fáciem tuam abscóndis, et arbitráris me inimícum tuum? Contra fólium, quod vento rápitur, osténdis poténtiam tuam, et stípulam siccam perséqueris: scribis enim contra me amaritúdines, et consúmere me vis peccátis adolescéntiæ meæ. Posuísti in nervo pedem meum, et observásti omnes sémitas meas, et vestígia pedum meórum considerásti: qui quasi putrédo consuméndus sum, et quasi vestiméntum quod coméditur a tínea.
parts.eng: Answer me. How many are my iniquities and sins? make me know my crimes and offences. Why hidest thou thy face, and thinkest me thy enemy? Against a leaf, that is carried away with the wind, thou showest thy power, and thou pursuest a dry straw. For thou writest bitter things against me, and wilt consume me for the sins of my youth. Thou hast put my feet in the stocks, and hast observed all my paths, and hast considered the steps of my feet: Who am to be consumed as rottenness, and as a garment that is moth-eaten.

parts.label: Tu autem
parts.lat: Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
parts.eng: But Thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

parts.label: Responsórium IV
parts.v1Lat:
℟. Meménto mei, Deus, quia ventus est vita mea,
* Nec aspíciat me visus hóminis.
parts.v1Eng:
℟. Remember, O God, that my life is wind.
* The eye of him that hath seen me shall see me no more.
parts.r1Lat: ℣. De profúndis clamávi ad te, Dómine: Dómine, exáudi vocem meam.
parts.r1Eng: ℣. Out of the depths have I cried unto thee, O Lord! Lord, hear my voice.
parts.r2Eng: ℟. The eye of him that hath seen me shall see me no more.

parts.label: Léctio V
parts.lat: Homo natus de mulíere, brevi vivens témpore, replétur multis misériis. Qui quasi flos egréditur et contéritur, et fugit velut umbra, et nunquam in eódem statu pérmanet. Et dignum ducis super hujuscémodi aperíre óculos tuos, et addúcere eum tecum in judícium? Quis potest fácere mundum de immúndo concéptum sémine? Nonne tu qui solus es? Breves dies hóminis sunt: númerus ménsium ejus apud te est: constituísti términos ejus, qui præteríri non póterunt. Recéde páululum ab eo, ut quiéscat, donec optáta véniat, sicut mercenárii, dies ejus.
parts.eng: Man born of a woman, living for a short time, is filled with many miseries. Who cometh forth like a flower, and is destroyed, and fleeth as a shadow, and never continueth in the same state. And dost thou think it meet to open thy eyes upon such an one, and to bring him into judgment with thee? Who can make him clean that is conceived of unclean seed? is it not thou who only art? The days of man are short, and the number of his months is with thee: thou hast appointed his bounds which cannot be passed. Depart a little from him, that he may rest, until his wished for day come, as that of the hireling.

parts.label: Tu autem
parts.lat: Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
parts.eng: But Thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

parts.label: Responsórium V
parts.v1Lat:
℟. Hei mihi, Dómine, quia peccávi nimis in vita mea: Quid fáciam, miser? ubi fúgiam, nisi ad te, Deus meus?
* Miserére mei, dum véneris in novíssimo die.
parts.v1Eng:
℟. Woe is me, O Lord! for I have sinned greatly in my life. I am smitten what shall I do? Whither shall I flee but unto thee, O my God?
* Have mercy upon me, when Thou comest at the latter day.
parts.r1Lat: ℣. Anima mea turbáta est valde, sed tu, Dómine, succúrre ei.
parts.r1Eng: ℣. My soul is sore vexed, but Thou, O Lord, help me.
parts.r2Lat: ℟. Miserére mei, dum véneris in novíssimo die.
parts.r2Eng: ℟. Have mercy upon me, when Thou comest at the latter day.

parts.label: Léctio VI
parts.lat: Quis mihi hoc tríbuat, ut in inférno prótegas me, et abscóndas me donec pertránseat furor tuus, et constítuas mihi tempus in quo recordéris mei? Putásne mórtuus homo rursum vivat? cunctis diébus quibus nunc mílito, expécto donec véniat immutátio mea. Vocábis me, et ego respondébo tibi: óperi mánuum tuárum porríges déxteram. Tu quidem gressus meos dinumerásti: sed parce peccátis meis.
parts.eng: Who will grant me this, that thou mayst protect me in hell, and hide me till thy wrath pass, and appoint me a time when thou wilt remember me? Shall man that is dead, thinkest thou, live again? all the days in which I am now in warfare, I expect until my change come. Thou shalt call me, and I will answer thee: to the work of thy hands thou shalt reach out thy right hand. Thou indeed hast numbered my steps, but spare my sins.

parts.label: Tu autem
parts.lat: Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
parts.eng: But Thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

parts.label: Responsórium VI
parts.v1Lat:
℟. Ne recordéris peccáta mea, Dómine,
* Dum véneris judicáre sǽculum per ignem.
parts.v1Eng:
℟. Hold not my sins in remembrance, O Lord,
* When thou comest to judge the world by fire.
parts.r1Lat: ℣. Dírige, Dómine, Deus meus, in conspéctu tuo viam meam.
parts.r1Eng: ℣. Make my way straight before thy face, O Lord my God.
parts.r2Lat:
℟. Dum véneris judicáre sǽculum per ignem.
℣. Réquiem ætérnam dona eis, Dómine: et lux perpétua lúceat eis.
℟. Dum véneris judicáre sǽculum per ignem.
parts.r2Eng:
℟. When thou comest to judge the world by fire.
℣. Eternal rest grant unto them, O Lord, and let perpetual light shine upon them.
℟. When thou comest to judge the world by fire.

parts.label: Psalmus 39
parts.antiphonLat: Compláceat * tibi, Dómine, ut erípias me: Dómine, ad adjuvándum me réspice.
parts.antiphonEng: Be pleased, O Lord, to deliver me * O Lord, look upon me to help me.

verses.lat: Exspéctans exspectávi Dóminum, * et inténdit mihi.
verses.eng: With expectation I have waited for the Lord, * and he was attentive to me.

verses.lat: Et exaudívit preces meas: * et edúxit me de lacu misériæ, et de luto fæcis.
verses.eng: And he heard my prayers, * and brought me out of the pit of misery and the mire of dregs.

verses.lat: Et státuit super petram pedes meos: * et diréxit gressus meos.
verses.eng: And he set my feet upon a rock, * and directed my steps.

verses.lat: Et immísit in os meum cánticum novum, * carmen Deo nostro.
verses.eng: And he put a new canticle into my mouth, * a song to our God.

verses.lat: Vidébunt multi, et timébunt: * et sperábunt in Dómino.
verses.eng: Many shall see, and shall fear: * and they shall hope in the Lord.

verses.lat: Beátus vir, cujus est nomen Dómini spes ejus: * et non respéxit in vanitátes et insánias falsas.
verses.eng: Blessed is the man whose trust is in the name of the Lord; * and who hath not had regard to vanities, and lying follies.

verses.lat: Multa fecísti tu, Dómine, Deus meus, mirabília tua: * et cogitatiónibus tuis non est qui símilis sit tibi.
verses.eng: Thou hast multiplied thy wonderful works, O Lord my God: * and in thy thoughts there is no one like to thee.

verses.lat: Annuntiávi et locútus sum: * multiplicáti sunt super númerum.
verses.eng: I have declared and I have spoken * they are multiplied above number.

verses.lat: Sacrifícium et oblatiónem noluísti: * aures autem perfecísti mihi.
verses.eng: Sacrifice and oblation thou didst not desire; * but thou hast pierced ears for me.

verses.lat: Holocáustum et pro peccáto non postulásti: * tunc dixi: Ecce, vénio.
verses.eng: Burnt offering and sin offering thou didst not require: * then said I, Behold I come.

verses.lat: In cápite libri scriptum est de me ut fácerem voluntátem tuam: * Deus meus, vólui, et legem tuam in médio cordis mei.
verses.eng: In the head of the book it is written of me that I should do thy will: * O my God, I have desired it, and thy law in the midst of my heart.

verses.lat: Annuntiávi justítiam tuam in ecclésia magna, * ecce, lábia mea non prohibébo: Dómine, tu scisti.
verses.eng: I have declared thy justice in a great church, * lo, I will not restrain my lips: O Lord, thou knowest it.

verses.lat: Justítiam tuam non abscóndi in corde meo: * veritátem tuam et salutáre tuum dixi.
verses.eng: I have not hid thy justice within my heart: * I have declared thy truth and thy salvation.

verses.lat: Non abscóndi misericórdiam tuam et veritátem tuam * a concílio multo.
verses.eng: I have not concealed thy mercy and thy truth * from a great council.

verses.lat: Tu autem, Dómine, ne longe fácias miseratiónes tuas a me: * misericórdia tua et véritas tua semper suscepérunt me.
verses.eng: Withhold not thou, O Lord, thy tender mercies from me: * thy mercy and thy truth have always upheld me.

verses.lat: Quóniam circumdedérunt me mala, quorum non est númerus: * comprehendérunt me iniquitátes meæ, et non pótui ut vidérem.
verses.eng: For evils without number have surrounded me; * my iniquities have overtaken me, and I was not able to see.

verses.lat: Multiplicátæ sunt super capíllos cápitis mei: * et cor meum derelíquit me.
verses.eng: They are multiplied above the hairs of my head: * and my heart hath forsaken me.

verses.lat: Compláceat tibi, Dómine, ut éruas me: * Dómine, ad adjuvándum me réspice.
verses.eng: Be pleased, O Lord to deliver me: * look down, O Lord, to help me.

verses.lat: Confundántur et revereántur simul, qui quærunt ánimam meam, * ut áuferant eam.
verses.eng: Let them be confounded and ashamed together, that seek after my soul * to take it away.

verses.lat: Convertántur retrórsum, et revereántur, * qui volunt mihi mala.
verses.eng: Let them be turned backward and be ashamed * that desire evils to me.

verses.lat: Ferant conféstim confusiónem suam, * qui dicunt mihi: Euge, euge.
verses.eng: Let them immediately bear their confusion, * that say to me: ’T is well, ’t is well.

verses.lat: Exsúltent et læténtur super te omnes quæréntes te: * et dicant semper: Magnificétur Dóminus: qui díligunt salutáre tuum.
verses.eng: Let all that seek thee rejoice and be glad in thee: * and let such as love thy salvation say always: The Lord be magnified.

verses.lat: Ego autem mendícus sum, et pauper: * Dóminus sollícitus est mei.
verses.eng: But I am a beggar and poor: * the Lord is careful for me.

verses.lat: Adjútor meus, et protéctor meus tu es: * Deus meus, ne tardáveris.
verses.eng: Thou art my helper and my protector: * O my God, be not slack.

verses.lat: Réquiem ætérnam * dona eis, Dómine.
verses.eng: Eternal rest * grant unto them, O Lord.

verses.lat: Et lux perpétua * lúceat eis.
verses.eng: And let perpetual light * shine upon them.

parts.rubric: Recited in full according to the Vulgate psalter; concluded with Réquiem ætérnam dona eis, Dómine: et lux perpétua lúceat eis, in place of Glória Patri.

parts.label: Psalmus 40
parts.antiphonLat: Sana, Dómine, * ánimam meam, quia peccávi tibi.
parts.antiphonEng: Lord, heal my soul; * for I have sinned against thee.

verses.lat: Beátus qui intéllegit super egénum, et páuperem: * in die mala liberábit eum Dóminus.
verses.eng: Blessed is he that understandeth concerning the needy and the poor: * the Lord will deliver him in the evil day.

verses.lat: Dóminus consérvet eum, et vivíficet eum, et beátum fáciat eum in terra: * et non tradat eum in ánimam inimicórum ejus.
verses.eng: The Lord preserve him and give him life, and make him blessed upon the earth: * and deliver him not up to the will of his enemies.

verses.lat: Dóminus opem ferat illi super lectum dolóris ejus: * univérsum stratum ejus versásti in infirmitáte ejus.
verses.eng: The Lord help him on his bed of sorrow: * thou hast turned all his couch in his sickness.

verses.lat: Ego dixi: Dómine, miserére mei: * sana ánimam meam, quia peccávi tibi.
verses.eng: I said: O Lord, be thou merciful to me: * heal my soul, for I have sinned against thee.

verses.lat: Inimíci mei dixérunt mala mihi: * Quando moriétur, et períbit nomen ejus?
verses.eng: My enemies have spoken evils against me: * when shall he die and his name perish?

verses.lat: Et si ingrediebátur ut vidéret, vana loquebátur: * cor ejus congregávit iniquitátem sibi.
verses.eng: And if he came in to see me, he spoke vain things: * his heart gathered together iniquity to itself.

verses.lat: Egrediebátur foras, * et loquebátur in idípsum.
verses.eng: He went out * and spoke to the same purpose.

verses.lat: Advérsum me susurrábant omnes inimíci mei: * advérsum me cogitábant mala mihi.
verses.eng: All my enemies whispered together against me: * they devised evils to me.

verses.lat: Verbum iníquum constituérunt advérsum me: * Numquid qui dormit non adíciet ut resúrgat?
verses.eng: They determined against me an unjust word: * shall he that sleepeth rise again no more?

verses.lat: Étenim homo pacis meæ, in quo sperávi: * qui edébat panes meos, magnificávit super me supplantatiónem.
verses.eng: For even the man of my peace, in whom I trusted, * who ate my bread, hath greatly supplanted me.

verses.lat: Tu autem, Dómine, miserére mei, et resúscita me: * et retríbuam eis.
verses.eng: But thou, O Lord, have mercy on me, and raise me up again: * and I will requite them.

verses.lat: In hoc cognóvi quóniam voluísti me: * quóniam non gaudébit inimícus meus super me.
verses.eng: By this I know, that thou hast had a good will for me: * because my enemy shall not rejoice over me.

verses.lat: Me autem propter innocéntiam suscepísti: * et confirmásti me in conspéctu tuo in ætérnum.
verses.eng: But thou hast upheld me by reason of my innocence: * and hast established me in thy sight for ever.

verses.lat: Benedíctus Dóminus, Deus Israël, a sǽculo et usque in sǽculum: * fiat, fiat.
verses.eng: Blessed be the Lord the God of Israel from eternity to eternity. * So be it. So be it.

verses.lat: Réquiem ætérnam * dona eis, Dómine.
verses.eng: Eternal rest * grant unto them, O Lord.

verses.lat: Et lux perpétua * lúceat eis.
verses.eng: And let perpetual light * shine upon them.

parts.rubric: Recited in full according to the Vulgate psalter; concluded with Réquiem ætérnam dona eis, Dómine: et lux perpétua lúceat eis, in place of Glória Patri.

parts.label: Psalmus 41
parts.antiphonLat: Sitívit * ánima mea ad Deum vivum: quando véniam, et apparébo ante fáciem Dómini?
parts.antiphonEng: My soul thirsteth for the living God; * when shall I come and appear before God?

verses.lat: Quemádmodum desíderat cervus ad fontes aquárum: * ita desíderat ánima mea ad te, Deus.
verses.eng: As the hart panteth after the fountains of water; * so my soul panteth after thee, O God.

verses.lat: Sitívit ánima mea ad Deum fortem vivum: * quando véniam, et apparébo ante fáciem Dei?
verses.eng: My soul hath thirsted after the strong living God; * when shall I come and appear before the face of God?

verses.lat: Fuérunt mihi lácrimæ meæ panes die ac nocte: * dum dícitur mihi cotídie: Ubi est Deus tuus?
verses.eng: My tears have been my bread day and night, * whilst it is said to me daily: Where is thy God?

verses.lat: Hæc recordátus sum, et effúdi in me ánimam meam: * quóniam transíbo in locum tabernáculi admirábilis, usque ad domum Dei.
verses.eng: These things I remembered, and poured out my soul in me: * for I shall go over into the place of the wonderful tabernacle, even to the house of God:

verses.lat: In voce exsultatiónis, et confessiónis: * sonus epulántis.
verses.eng: With the voice of joy and praise; * the noise of one feasting.

verses.lat: Quare tristis es, ánima mea? * et quare contúrbas me?
verses.eng: Why art thou sad, O my soul? * and why dost thou trouble me?

verses.lat: Spera in Deo, quóniam adhuc confitébor illi: * salutáre vultus mei, et Deus meus.
verses.eng: Hope in God, for I will still give praise to him: * the salvation of my countenance, and my God.

verses.lat: Ad meípsum ánima mea conturbáta est: * proptérea memor ero tui de terra Jordánis, et Hermóniim a monte módico.
verses.eng: My soul is troubled within myself: * therefore will I remember thee from the land of Jordan and Hermoniim, from the little hill.

verses.lat: Abýssus abýssum ínvocat, * in voce cataractárum tuárum.
verses.eng: Deep calleth on deep, * at the noise of thy flood-gates.

verses.lat: Ómnia excélsa tua, et fluctus tui * super me transiérunt.
verses.eng: All thy heights and thy billows * have passed over me.

verses.lat: In die mandávit Dóminus misericórdiam suam: * et nocte cánticum ejus.
verses.eng: In the daytime the Lord hath commanded his mercy; * and a canticle to him in the night.

verses.lat: Apud me orátio Deo vitæ meæ, * dicam Deo: Suscéptor meus es.
verses.eng: With me is prayer to the God of my life. * I will say to God: Thou art my support.

verses.lat: Quare oblítus es mei? * et quare contristátus incédo, dum afflígit me inimícus?
verses.eng: Why hast thou forgotten me? * and why go I mourning, whilst my enemy afflicteth me?

verses.lat: Dum confringúntur ossa mea, * exprobravérunt mihi qui tríbulant me inimíci mei.
verses.eng: Whilst my bones are broken, * my enemies who trouble me have reproached me;

verses.lat: Dum dicunt mihi per síngulos dies: Ubi est Deus tuus? * quare tristis es, ánima mea? et quare contúrbas me?
verses.eng: Whilst they say to me day by day: Where is thy God? * Why art thou cast down, O my soul? and why dost thou disquiet me?

verses.lat: Spera in Deo, quóniam adhuc confitébor illi: * salutáre vultus mei, et Deus meus.
verses.eng: Hope thou in God, for I will still give praise to him: * the salvation of my countenance, and my God.

verses.lat: Réquiem ætérnam * dona eis, Dómine.
verses.eng: Eternal rest * grant unto them, O Lord.

verses.lat: Et lux perpétua * lúceat eis.
verses.eng: And let perpetual light * shine upon them.

parts.rubric: Recited in full according to the Vulgate psalter; concluded with Réquiem ætérnam dona eis, Dómine: et lux perpétua lúceat eis, in place of Glória Patri.

parts.label: Versicle after Nocturn III
parts.lat: ℣. Ne tradas béstiis ánimas confiténtes tibi.
parts.eng: ℣. O deliver not unto beasts the souls of them that praise thee!
parts.latR: ℟. Et ánimas páuperum tuórum ne obliviscáris in finem.
parts.engR: ℟. And forget not the souls of thy poor for ever.

parts.label: Pater Noster (silently)
parts.lat: Pater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum. Advéniat regnum tuum. Fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum quotidiánum da nobis hódie, et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris. Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem, sed líbera nos a malo. Amen.
parts.eng: Our Father, who art in heaven, hallowed be Thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth, as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread, and forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us. And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil. Amen.
parts.rubric: Said silently.

parts.label: Léctio VII
parts.lat: Spíritus meus attenuábitur; dies mei breviabúntur: et solum mihi súperest sepúlchrum. Non peccávi, et in amaritudínibus morátur óculus meus. Líbera me, Dómine, et pone me juxta te, et cujúsvis manus pugnet contra me. Dies mei transiérunt; cogitatiónes meæ dissipátæ sunt, torquéntes cor meum. Noctem vertérunt in diem, et rursum post ténebras spero lucem. Si sustinúero, inférnus domus mea est, et in ténebris stravi léctulum meum. Putrédini dixi: Pater meus es; Mater mea, et soror mea, vérmibus. Ubi est ergo nunc præstolátio mea? et patiéntiam meam quis consíderat?
parts.eng: My spirit shall be wasted, my days shall be shortened, and only the grave remaineth for me. I have not sinned, and my eye abideth in bitterness. Deliver me O Lord, and set me beside thee, and let any man's hand fight against me. My days have passed away, my thoughts are dissipated, tormenting my heart. They have turned night into day, and after darkness I hope for light again. If I wait hell is my house, and I have made my bed in darkness. If I have said to rottenness: thou art my father; to worms, my mother and my sister. Where is now then my expectation, and who considereth my patience?

parts.label: Tu autem
parts.lat: Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
parts.eng: But Thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

parts.label: Responsórium VII
parts.v1Lat:
℟. Peccántem me cotídie, et non me pœniténtem, timor mortis contúrbat me:
* Quia in inférno nulla est redémptio, miserére mei, Deus, et salva me.
parts.v1Eng:
℟. Forasmuch as I sin daily, and repent not, the fear of death troubleth me.
* O God, have mercy upon me, and save me, for in hell there is no redemption.
parts.r1Lat: ℣. Deus, in nómine tuo salvum me fac, et in virtúte tua líbera me.
parts.r1Eng: ℣. Save me, O God, by thy name, and judge me in thy strength.
parts.r2Lat: ℟. Quia in inférno nulla est redémptio, miserére mei, Deus, et salva me.
parts.r2Eng: ℟. O God, have mercy upon me, and save me, for in hell there is no redemption.

parts.label: Léctio VIII
parts.lat: Pelli meæ, consúmptis cárnibus, adhǽsit os meum, et derelícta sunt tantúmmodo lábia circa dentes meos. Miserémini mei, miserémini mei saltem vos, amíci mei, quia manus Dómini tétigit me. Quare persequímini me sicut Deus, et cárnibus meis saturámini? Quis mihi tríbuat ut scribántur sermónes mei? quis mihi det ut exaréntur in libro stylo férreo et plumbi lámina, vel celte sculpántur in sílice? Scio enim quod redémptor meus vivit, et in novíssimo die de terra surrectúrus sum: et rursum circúmdabor pelle mea, et in carne mea vidébo Deum meum: quem visúrus sum ego ipse, et óculi mei conspectúri sunt, et non álius: repósita est hæc spes mea in sinu meo.
parts.eng: The flesh being consumed. My bone hath cleaved to my skin, and nothing but lips are left about my teeth. Have pity on me, have pity on me, at least you my friends, because the hand of the Lord hath touched me. Why do you persecute me as God, and glut yourselves with my flesh? Who will grant me that my words may be written? Who will grant me that they may be marked down in a book? With an iron pen and in a plate of lead, or else be graven with an instrument in flint stone. For I know that my Redeemer liveth, and in the last day I shall rise out of the earth. And I shall be clothed again with my skin, and in my flesh I will see my God. Whom I myself shall see, and my eyes shall behold, and not another: this my hope is laid up in my bosom.

parts.label: Tu autem
parts.lat: Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
parts.eng: But Thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

parts.label: Responsórium VIII
parts.v1Lat:
℟. Dómine, secúndum actum meum noli me judicáre: nihil dignum in conspéctu tuo egi; ídeo déprecor majestátem tuam,
* Ut tu, Deus, déleas iniquitátem meam.
parts.v1Eng:
℟. O Lord, judge me not according to my works; for I have done nothing that can be counted in respect of thee. I beseech thy majesty therefore, that thou wouldest
* Blot out my transgressions, O God.
parts.r1Lat: ℣. Amplius lava me, Dómine, ab injustítia mea, et a delícto meo munda me.
parts.r1Eng: ℣. Lord, wash me thoroughly from mine iniquity and cleanse me from my sin.
parts.r2Lat: ℟. Ut tu, Deus, déleas iniquitátem meam.
parts.r2Eng: ℟. Blot out my transgressions, O God.

parts.label: Léctio IX
parts.lat: Quare de vulva eduxísti me? qui útinam consúmptus essem, ne óculus me vidéret. Fuíssem quasi non essem, de útero translátus ad túmulum. Numquid non páucitas diérum meórum finiétur brevi? dimítte ergo me, ut plangam páululum dolórem meum, ántequam vadam, et non revértar, ad terram tenebrósam, et opértam mortis calígine: terram misériæ et tenebrárum, ubi umbra mortis et nullus ordo, sed sempitérnus horror inhábitat.
parts.eng: Why didst thou bring me forth out of the womb: O that I had been consumed that eye might not see me! I should have been as if I had not been, carried from the womb to the grave. Shall not the fewness of my days be ended shortly? suffer me, therefore, that I may lament my sorrow a little: Before I go, and return no more, to a land that is dark and covered with the mist of death: A land of misery and darkness, where the shadow of death, and no order, but everlasting horror dwelleth.

parts.label: Tu autem
parts.lat: Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
parts.eng: But Thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

parts.label: Responsórium IX
parts.v1Lat:
℟. Líbera me, Dómine, de morte ætérna in die illa treménda,
* Quando cæli movéndi sunt et terra,
* Dum véneris judicáre sǽculum per ignem.
parts.r1Lat:
℣. Tremens factus sum ego et tímeo, dum discússio vénerit atque ventúra ira.
℟. Quando cæli movéndi sunt et terra.
℣. Dies illa, dies iræ, calamitátis et misériæ, dies magna et amára valde.
℟. Dum véneris judicáre sǽculum per ignem.
℣. Réquiem ætérnam dona eis, Dómine: et lux perpétua lúceat eis.
parts.r1Eng:
℣. Quaking and dread take hold upon me, when I look for the coming of the trial and the wrath to come.
℟. When the heavens and the earth shall be shaken.
℣. That day is a day of wrath, of wasteness and desolation, a great day and exceeding bitter.
℟. When Thou shalt come to judge the world by fire.
℣. Eternal rest grant unto them, O Lord, and let perpetual light shine upon them.
parts.r2Lat: ℟. Líbera me, Dómine, de morte ætérna in die illa treménda, * Quando cæli movéndi sunt et terra, * Dum véneris judicáre sǽculum per ignem.
parts.r2Eng: ℟. Deliver me, O Lord, from eternal death in that awful day, when the heavens and the earth shall be shaken, and Thou shalt come to judge the world by fire.

parts.label: Conclusio
parts.lat: Réquiem ætérnam dona eis, Dómine.
parts.eng: O Lord, grant them eternal rest.
parts.engR: And let the everlasting light shine upon them.

parts.label: Conclusio (continued)
parts.lat: Requiéscant in pace.
parts.eng: May they rest in peace.

parts.label: Pater Noster, Ave María (silently)
parts.lat:
Pater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum. Advéniat regnum tuum. Fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum quotidiánum da nobis hódie, et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris. Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem, sed líbera nos a malo. Amen.

Ave María, grátia plena, Dóminus tecum. Benedícta tu in muliéribus, et benedíctus fructus ventris tui, Jesus. Sancta María, Mater Dei, ora pro nobis peccatóribus, nunc et in hora mortis nostræ. Amen.
parts.eng:
Our Father, who art in heaven, hallowed be Thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth, as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread, and forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us. And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil. Amen.

Hail Mary, full of grace, the Lord is with thee. Blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb, Jesus. Holy Mary, Mother of God, pray for us sinners, now and at the hour of our death. Amen.
parts.rubric: Said silently.

parts.label: Psalmus 50; Miserére mei
parts.antiphonLat: Exsultábunt Dómino * ossa humiliáta.
parts.antiphonEng: The bones which thou hast broken * may rejoice.

verses.lat: Miserére mei, Deus, * secúndum magnam misericórdiam tuam.
verses.eng: Have mercy on me, O God, * according to thy great mercy.

verses.lat: Et secúndum multitúdinem miseratiónum tuárum, * dele iniquitátem meam.
verses.eng: And according to the multitude of thy tender mercies * blot out my iniquity.

verses.lat: Ámplius lava me ab iniquitáte mea: * et a peccáto meo munda me.
verses.eng: Wash me yet more from my iniquity, * and cleanse me from my sin.

verses.lat: Quóniam iniquitátem meam ego cognósco: * et peccátum meum contra me est semper.
verses.eng: For I know my iniquity, * and my sin is always before me.

verses.lat: Tibi soli peccávi, et malum coram te feci: * ut justificéris in sermónibus tuis, et vincas cum judicáris.
verses.eng: To thee only have I sinned, and have done evil before thee: * that thou mayst be justified in thy words, and mayst overcome when thou art judged.

verses.lat: Ecce enim, in iniquitátibus concéptus sum: * et in peccátis concépit me mater mea.
verses.eng: For behold I was conceived in iniquities; * and in sins did my mother conceive me.

verses.lat: Ecce enim, veritátem dilexísti: * incérta et occúlta sapiéntiæ tuæ manifestásti mihi.
verses.eng: For behold thou hast loved truth: * the uncertain and hidden things of thy wisdom thou hast made manifest to me.

verses.lat: Aspérges me hyssópo, et mundábor: * lavábis me, et super nivem dealbábor.
verses.eng: Thou shalt sprinkle me with hyssop, and I shall be cleansed: * thou shalt wash me, and I shall be made whiter than snow.

verses.lat: Audítui meo dabis gáudium et lætítiam: * et exsultábunt ossa humiliáta.
verses.eng: To my hearing thou shalt give joy and gladness: * and the bones that have been humbled shall rejoice.

verses.lat: Avérte fáciem tuam a peccátis meis: * et omnes iniquitátes meas dele.
verses.eng: Turn away thy face from my sins, * and blot out all my iniquities.

verses.lat: Cor mundum crea in me, Deus: * et spíritum rectum ínnova in viscéribus meis.
verses.eng: Create a clean heart in me, O God: * and renew a right spirit within my bowels.

verses.lat: Ne proícias me a fácie tua: * et spíritum sanctum tuum ne áuferas a me.
verses.eng: Cast me not away from thy face; * and take not thy holy spirit from me.

verses.lat: Redde mihi lætítiam salutáris tui: * et spíritu principáli confírma me.
verses.eng: Restore unto me the joy of thy salvation, * and strengthen me with a perfect spirit.

verses.lat: Docébo iníquos vias tuas: * et ímpii ad te converténtur.
verses.eng: I will teach the unjust thy ways: * and the wicked shall be converted to thee.

verses.lat: Líbera me de sanguínibus, Deus, Deus salútis meæ: * et exsultábit lingua mea justítiam tuam.
verses.eng: Deliver me from blood, O God, thou God of my salvation: * and my tongue shall extol thy justice.

verses.lat: Dómine, lábia mea apéries: * et os meum annuntiábit laudem tuam.
verses.eng: O Lord, thou wilt open my lips: * and my mouth shall declare thy praise.

verses.lat: Quóniam si voluísses sacrifícium, dedíssem útique: * holocáustis non delectáberis.
verses.eng: For if thou hadst desired sacrifice, I would indeed have given it: * with burnt offerings thou wilt not be delighted.

verses.lat: Sacrifícium Deo spíritus contribulátus: * cor contrítum, et humiliátum, Deus, non despícies.
verses.eng: A sacrifice to God is an afflicted spirit: * a contrite and humbled heart, O God, thou wilt not despise.

verses.lat: Benígne fac, Dómine, in bona voluntáte tua Sion: * ut ædificéntur muri Jerúsalem.
verses.eng: Deal favourably, O Lord, in thy good will with Sion; * that the walls of Jerusalem may be built up.

verses.lat: Tunc acceptábis sacrifícium justítiæ, oblatiónes, et holocáusta: * tunc impónent super altáre tuum vítulos.
verses.eng: Then shalt thou accept the sacrifice of justice, oblations and whole burnt offerings: * then shall they lay calves upon thy altar.

verses.lat: Réquiem ætérnam * dona eis, Dómine.
verses.eng: Eternal rest * grant unto them, O Lord.

verses.lat: Et lux perpétua * lúceat eis.
verses.eng: And let perpetual light * shine upon them.

parts.rubric: Recited in full according to the Vulgate psalter; concluded with Réquiem ætérnam dona eis, Dómine: et lux perpétua lúceat eis, in place of Glória Patri.

parts.label: Psalmus 64; Te decet hymnus
parts.antiphonLat: Exáudi, Dómine, * oratiónem meam: ad te omnis caro véniet.
parts.antiphonEng: Lord, hear * my prayer; unto thee shall all flesh come.

verses.lat: Te decet hymnus, Deus, in Sion: * et tibi reddétur votum in Jerúsalem.
verses.eng: A hymn, O God, becometh thee in Sion: * and a vow shall be paid to thee in Jerusalem.

verses.lat: Exáudi oratiónem meam: * ad te omnis caro véniet.
verses.eng: O hear my prayer: * all flesh shall come to thee.

verses.lat: Verba iniquórum prævaluérunt super nos: * et impietátibus nostris tu propitiáberis.
verses.eng: The words of the wicked have prevailed over us: * and thou wilt pardon our transgressions.

verses.lat: Beátus, quem elegísti, et assumpsísti: * inhabitábit in átriis tuis.
verses.eng: Blessed is he whom thou hast chosen and taken to thee: * he shall dwell in thy courts.

verses.lat: Replébimur in bonis domus tuæ: * sanctum est templum tuum, mirábile in æquitáte.
verses.eng: We shall be filled with the good things of thy house; holy is thy temple, * wonderful in justice.

verses.lat: Exáudi nos, Deus, salutáris noster, * spes ómnium fínium terræ, et in mari longe.
verses.eng: Hear us, O God our saviour, * who art the hope of all the ends of the earth, and in the sea afar off.

verses.lat: Prǽparans montes in virtúte tua, accínctus poténtia: * qui contúrbas profúndum maris sonum flúctuum ejus.
verses.eng: Thou who preparest the mountains by thy strength, being girded with power: * who troublest the depth of the sea, the noise of its waves.

verses.lat: Turbabúntur gentes, et timébunt qui hábitant términos a signis tuis: * éxitus matutíni, et véspere delectábis.
verses.eng: The Gentiles shall be troubled, and they that dwell in the uttermost borders shall be afraid at thy signs: * thou shalt make the outgoings of the morning and of the evening to be joyful.

verses.lat: Visitásti terram, et inebriásti eam: * multiplicásti locupletáre eam.
verses.eng: Thou hast visited the earth, and hast plentifully watered it; * thou hast many ways enriched it.

verses.lat: Flumen Dei replétum est aquis, parásti cibum illórum: * quóniam ita est præparátio ejus.
verses.eng: The river of God is filled with water, thou hast prepared their food; * for so is its preparation.

verses.lat: Rivos ejus inébria, multíplica genímina ejus: * in stillicídiis ejus lætábitur gérminans.
verses.eng: Fill up plentifully the streams thereof, multiply its fruits; * it shall spring up and rejoice in its showers.

verses.lat: Benedíces corónæ anni benignitátis tuæ: * et campi tui replebúntur ubertáte.
verses.eng: Thou shalt bless the crown of the year of thy goodness: * and thy fields shall be filled with plenty.

verses.lat: Pinguéscent speciósa desérti: * et exsultatióne colles accingéntur.
verses.eng: The beautiful places of the wilderness shall grow fat: * and the hills shall be girded about with joy.

verses.lat: Indúti sunt aríetes óvium, et valles abundábunt fruménto: * clamábunt, étenim hymnum dicent.
verses.eng: The rams of the flock are clothed, and the vales shall abound with corn: * they shall shout, yea they shall sing a hymn.

verses.lat: Réquiem ætérnam * dona eis, Dómine.
verses.eng: Eternal rest * grant unto them, O Lord.

verses.lat: Et lux perpétua * lúceat eis.
verses.eng: And let perpetual light * shine upon them.

parts.rubric: Recited in full according to the Vulgate psalter; concluded with Réquiem ætérnam dona eis, Dómine: et lux perpétua lúceat eis, in place of Glória Patri.

parts.label: Psalmi 62 & 66; Deus, Deus meus / Deus misereátur
parts.antiphonLat: Me suscépit * déxtera tua, Dómine.
parts.antiphonEng: Thy right hand * upholdeth me.

verses.lat: Deus, Deus meus, * ad te de luce vígilo.
verses.eng: O God, my God, * to thee do I watch at break of day.

verses.lat: Sitívit in te ánima mea, * quam multiplíciter tibi caro mea.
verses.eng: For thee my soul hath thirsted; * for thee my flesh, O how many ways!

verses.lat: In terra desérta, et ínvia, et inaquósa: ‡ sic in sancto appárui tibi, * ut vidérem virtútem tuam, et glóriam tuam.
verses.eng: In a desert land, and where there is no way, and no water: ‡ so in the sanctuary have I come before thee, * to see thy power and thy glory.

verses.lat: Quóniam mélior est misericórdia tua super vitas: * lábia mea laudábunt te.
verses.eng: For thy mercy is better than lives: * thee my lips shall praise.

verses.lat: Sic benedícam te in vita mea: * et in nómine tuo levábo manus meas.
verses.eng: Thus will I bless thee all my life long: * and in thy name I will lift up my hands.

verses.lat: Sicut ádipe et pinguédine repleátur ánima mea: * et lábiis exsultatiónis laudábit os meum.
verses.eng: Let my soul be filled as with marrow and fatness: * and my mouth shall praise thee with joyful lips.

verses.lat: Si memor fui tui super stratum meum, † in matutínis meditábor in te: * (8a) quia fuísti adjútor meus.
verses.eng: If I have remembered thee upon my bed, † I will meditate on thee in the morning: * (8a) because thou hast been my helper.

verses.lat: Et in velaménto alárum tuárum exsultábo, † (9) adhǽsit ánima mea post te: * me suscépit déxtera tua.
verses.eng: And I will rejoice under the covert of thy wings: † my soul hath stuck close to thee: * (9) thy right hand hath received me.

verses.lat: Ipsi vero in vanum quæsiérunt ánimam meam, † introíbunt in inferióra terræ: * (11) tradéntur in manus gládii, partes vúlpium erunt.
verses.eng: But they have sought my soul in vain, † they shall go into the lower parts of the earth: * (11) they shall be delivered into the hands of the sword, they shall be the portions of foxes.

verses.lat: Rex vero lætábitur in Deo, † laudabúntur omnes qui jurant in eo: * quia obstrúctum est os loquéntium iníqua.
verses.eng: But the king shall rejoice in God, all they shall be praised that swear by him: * because the mouth is stopped of them that speak wicked things.

verses.lat: Deus misereátur nostri, et benedícat nobis: * illúminet vultum suum super nos, et misereátur nostri.
verses.eng: May God have mercy on us, and bless us: * may he cause the light of his countenance to shine upon us, and may he have mercy on us.

verses.lat: Ut cognoscámus in terra viam tuam, * in ómnibus géntibus salutáre tuum.
verses.eng: That we may know thy way upon earth: * thy salvation in all nations.

verses.lat: Confiteántur tibi pópuli, Deus: * confiteántur tibi pópuli omnes.
verses.eng: Let people confess to thee, O God: * let all people give praise to thee.

verses.lat: Læténtur et exsúltent gentes: * quóniam júdicas pópulos in æquitáte, et gentes in terra dírigis.
verses.eng: Let the nations be glad and rejoice: * for thou judgest the people with justice, and directest the nations upon earth.

verses.lat: Confiteántur tibi pópuli, Deus, confiteántur tibi pópuli omnes: * (7a) terra dedit fructum suum.
verses.eng: Let the people, O God, confess to thee: * (7a) let all the people give praise to thee: the earth hath yielded her fruit.

verses.lat: Benedícat nos Deus, Deus noster, (8) benedícat nos Deus: * et métuant eum omnes fines terræ.
verses.eng: May God, our God bless us, (8) may God bless us: * and all the ends of the earth fear him.

verses.lat: Réquiem ætérnam * dona eis, Dómine.
verses.eng: Eternal rest * grant unto them, O Lord.

verses.lat: Et lux perpétua * lúceat eis.
verses.eng: And let perpetual light * shine upon them.

parts.rubric: Recited in full according to the Vulgate psalter; concluded with Réquiem ætérnam dona eis, Dómine: et lux perpétua lúceat eis, in place of Glória Patri.

parts.label: Canticum Ezechíæ (Isaías 38:10-20); Ego dixi
parts.antiphonLat: A porta ínferi * érue, Dómine, ánimam meam.
parts.antiphonEng: From the gates of hell * deliver my soul, O Lord.

verses.lat: Ego dixi: In dimídio diérum meórum * vadam ad portas ínferi.
verses.eng: I said: In the midst of my days * I shall go to the gates of hell:

verses.lat: Quæsívi resíduum annórum meórum. * Dixi: Non vidébo Dóminum Deum in terra vivéntium.
verses.eng: I sought for the residue of my years. * I said: I shall not see the Lord God in the land of the living.

verses.lat: Non aspíciam hóminem ultra, * et habitatórem quiétis.
verses.eng: I shall behold man no more, * nor the inhabitant of rest.

verses.lat: Generátio mea abláta est, et convolúta est a me, * quasi tabernáculum pastórum.
verses.eng: My generation is at an end, and it is rolled away from me, * as a shepherd’s tent.

verses.lat: Præcísa est velut a texénte, vita mea: dum adhuc ordírer, succídit me: * de mane usque ad vésperam fínies me.
verses.eng: My life is cut off, as by a weaver: whilst I was yet but beginning, he cut me off: * from morning even to night thou wilt make an end of me.

verses.lat: Sperábam usque ad mane, * quasi leo sic contrívit ómnia ossa mea:
verses.eng: I hoped till morning, * as a lion so hath he broken all my bones:

verses.lat: De mane usque ad vésperam fínies me: * sicut pullus hirúndinis sic clamábo, meditábor ut colúmba:
verses.eng: From morning even to night thou wilt make an end of me. * I will cry like a young swallow, I will meditate like a dove:

verses.lat: Attenuáti sunt óculi mei, * suspiciéntes in excélsum.
verses.eng: My eyes are weakened * looking upward:

verses.lat: Dómine, vim pátior, respónde pro me. * Quid dicam, aut quid respondébit mihi, cum ipse fécerit?
verses.eng: Lord, I suffer violence, answer thou for me. * What shall I say, or what shall he answer for me, whereas he himself hath done it?

verses.lat: Recogitábo tibi omnes annos meos * in amaritúdine ánimæ meæ.
verses.eng: I will recount to thee all my years * in the bitterness of my soul.

verses.lat: Dómine, si sic vívitur, et in tálibus vita spíritus mei, corrípies me, et vivificábis me. * Ecce, in pace amaritúdo mea amaríssima:
verses.eng: O Lord, if man’s life be such, and the life of my spirit be in such things as these, thou shalt correct me, and make me to live. * Behold in peace is my bitterness most bitter:

verses.lat: Tu autem eruísti ánimam meam ut non períret: * projecísti post tergum tuum ómnia peccáta mea.
verses.eng: But thou hast delivered my soul that it should not perish, * thou hast cast all my sins behind thy back.

verses.lat: Quia non inférnus confitébitur tibi, neque mors laudábit te: * non exspectábunt qui descéndunt in lacum, veritátem tuam.
verses.eng: For hell shall not confess to thee, neither shall death praise thee: * nor shall they that go down into the pit, look for thy truth.

verses.lat: Vivens vivens ipse confitébitur tibi, sicut et ego hódie: * pater fíliis notam fáciet veritátem tuam.
verses.eng: The living, the living, he shall give praise to thee, as I do this day: * the father shall make thy truth known to the children.

verses.lat: Dómine, salvum me fac * et psalmos nostros cantábimus cunctis diébus vitæ nostræ in domo Dómini.
verses.eng: O Lord, save me, and we will sing our psalms all the days of our life * in the house of the Lord.

verses.lat: Réquiem ætérnam * dona eis, Dómine.
verses.eng: Eternal rest * grant unto them, O Lord.

verses.lat: Et lux perpétua * lúceat eis.
verses.eng: And let perpetual light * shine upon them.

parts.rubric: Recited in full according to the Vulgate psalter; concluded with Réquiem ætérnam dona eis, Dómine: et lux perpétua lúceat eis, in place of Glória Patri.

parts.label: Psalmi 148, 149, 150; Laudate Dóminum
parts.antiphonLat: Omnis spíritus * laudet Dóminum.
parts.antiphonEng: Let everything that hath breath * praise the Lord.

verses.lat: Laudáte Dóminum de cælis: * laudáte eum in excélsis.
verses.eng: Praise ye the Lord from the heavens * praise ye him in the high places.

verses.lat: Laudáte eum, omnes Ángeli ejus: * laudáte eum, omnes virtútes ejus.
verses.eng: Praise ye him, all his angels: * praise ye him, all his hosts.

verses.lat: Laudáte eum, sol et luna: * laudáte eum, omnes stellæ et lumen.
verses.eng: Praise ye him, O sun and moon: * praise him, all ye stars and light.

verses.lat: Laudáte eum, cæli cælórum: * et aquæ omnes, quæ super cælos sunt, laudent nomen Dómini.
verses.eng: Praise him, ye heavens of heavens: * and let all the waters that are above the heavens, praise the name of the Lord.

verses.lat: Quia ipse dixit, et facta sunt: * ipse mandávit, et creáta sunt.
verses.eng: For he spoke, and they were made: * he commanded, and they were created.

verses.lat: Státuit ea in ætérnum, et in sǽculum sǽculi: * præcéptum pósuit, et non præteríbit.
verses.eng: He hath established them for ever, and for ages of ages: * he hath made a decree, and it shall not pass away.

verses.lat: Laudáte Dóminum de terra, * dracónes, et omnes abýssi.
verses.eng: Praise the Lord from the earth, * ye dragons, and all ye deeps:

verses.lat: Ignis, grando, nix, glácies, spíritus procellárum: * quæ fáciunt verbum ejus:
verses.eng: Fire, hail, snow, ice, stormy winds * which fulfill his word:

verses.lat: Montes, et omnes colles: * ligna fructífera, et omnes cedri.
verses.eng: Mountains and all hills, * fruitful trees and all cedars:

verses.lat: Béstiæ, et univérsa pécora: * serpéntes, et vólucres pennátæ:
verses.eng: Beasts and all cattle: * serpents and feathered fowls:

verses.lat: Reges terræ, et omnes pópuli: * príncipes, et omnes júdices terræ.
verses.eng: Kings of the earth and all people: * princes and all judges of the earth:

verses.lat: Júvenes, et vírgines: † senes cum junióribus laudent nomen Dómini: * (13) quia exaltátum est nomen ejus solíus.
verses.eng: Young men and maidens: † let the old with the younger, praise the name of the Lord: * (13) For his name alone is exalted.

verses.lat: Conféssio ejus super cælum et terram: * et exaltávit cornu pópuli sui.
verses.eng: The praise of him is above heaven and earth: * and he hath exalted the horn of his people.

verses.lat: Hymnus ómnibus sanctis ejus: * fíliis Israël, pópulo appropinquánti sibi.
verses.eng: A hymn to all his saints: to the children of Israel, a people approaching him.

verses.lat: Cantáte Dómino cánticum novum: * laus ejus in ecclésia sanctórum.
verses.eng: Sing ye to the Lord a new canticle: * let his praise be in the church of the saints.

verses.lat: Lætétur Israël in eo, qui fecit eum: * et fílii Sion exsúltent in rege suo.
verses.eng: Let Israel rejoice in him that made him: * and let the children of Sion be joyful in their king.

verses.lat: Laudent nomen ejus in choro: * in týmpano, et psaltério psallant ei:
verses.eng: Let them praise his name in choir: * let them sing to him with the timbrel and the psaltery.

verses.lat: Quia beneplácitum est Dómino in pópulo suo: * et exaltábit mansuétos in salútem.
verses.eng: For the Lord is well pleased with his people: * and he will exalt the meek unto salvation.

verses.lat: Exsultábunt sancti in glória: * lætabúntur in cubílibus suis.
verses.eng: The saints shall rejoice in glory: * they shall be joyful in their beds.

verses.lat: Exaltatiónes Dei in gútture eórum: * et gládii ancípites in mánibus eórum.
verses.eng: The high praises of God shall be in their mouth: * and two-edged swords in their hands:

verses.lat: Ad faciéndam vindíctam in natiónibus: * increpatiónes in pópulis.
verses.eng: To execute vengeance upon the nations, * chastisements among the people:

verses.lat: Ad alligándos reges eórum in compédibus: * et nóbiles eórum in mánicis férreis.
verses.eng: To bind their kings with fetters, * and their nobles with manacles of iron.

verses.lat: Ut fáciant in eis judícium conscríptum: * glória hæc est ómnibus sanctis ejus.
verses.eng: To execute upon them the judgment that is written: * this glory is to all his saints.

verses.lat: Laudáte Dóminum in sanctis ejus: * laudáte eum in firmaménto virtútis ejus.
verses.eng: Praise ye the Lord in his holy places: * praise ye him in the firmament of his power.

verses.lat: Laudáte eum in virtútibus ejus: * laudáte eum secúndum multitúdinem magnitúdinis ejus.
verses.eng: Praise ye him for his mighty acts: * praise ye him according to the multitude of his greatness.

verses.lat: Laudáte eum in sono tubæ: * laudáte eum in psaltério, et cíthara.
verses.eng: Praise him with sound of trumpet: * praise him with psaltery and harp.

verses.lat: Laudáte eum in týmpano, et choro: * laudáte eum in chordis, et órgano.
verses.eng: Praise him with timbrel and choir: * praise him with strings and organs.

verses.lat: Laudáte eum in cýmbalis benesonántibus: † laudáte eum in cýmbalis jubilatiónis: * (6) omnis spíritus laudet Dóminum.
verses.eng: Praise him on high sounding cymbals: † praise him on cymbals of joy: * (6) let every spirit praise the Lord.

verses.lat: Réquiem ætérnam * dona eis, Dómine.
verses.eng: Eternal rest * grant unto them, O Lord.

verses.lat: Et lux perpétua * lúceat eis.
verses.eng: And let perpetual light * shine upon them.

parts.rubric: Recited in full according to the Vulgate psalter; concluded with Réquiem ætérnam dona eis, Dómine: et lux perpétua lúceat eis, in place of Glória Patri.

parts.label: Versicle
parts.lat: Audívi vocem de cælo dicéntem mihi.
parts.eng: I heard a voice from heaven, saying unto me:
parts.latR: Beáti mórtui qui in Dómino moriúntur.
parts.engR: Blessed are the dead which die in the Lord.

parts.label: Antiphon ad Benedíctus
parts.lat: Ego sum * resurréctio et vita: qui credit in me, étiam si mórtuus fúerit, vivet; et omnis qui vivit et credit in me, non moriétur in ætérnum.
parts.eng: I am the resurrection and the life: * he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live; and whosoever liveth and believeth in me shall never die.

verses.lat: Benedíctus Dóminus, Deus Israël, * quia visitávit, et fecit redemptiónem plebis suæ:
verses.eng: Blessed be the Lord God of Israel; * because He hath visited and wrought the redemption of His people:

verses.lat: Et eréxit cornu salútis nobis: * in domo David, púeri sui.
verses.eng: And hath raised up an horn of salvation to us, * in the house of David His servant:

verses.lat: Sicut locútus est per os sanctórum, * qui a sǽculo sunt, prophetárum ejus:
verses.eng: As He spoke by the mouth of His holy Prophets, * who are from the beginning:

verses.lat: Salútem ex inimícis nostris, * et de manu ómnium, qui odérunt nos.
verses.eng: Salvation from our enemies, * and from the hand of all that hate us.

verses.lat: Ad faciéndam misericórdiam cum pátribus nostris: * et memorári testaménti sui sancti.
verses.eng: To perform mercy to our fathers, * and to remember His holy testament.

verses.lat: Jusjurándum, quod jurávit ad Abraham patrem nostrum, * datúrum se nobis:
verses.eng: The oath, which He swore to Abraham our father, * that He would grant to us.

verses.lat: Ut sine timóre, de manu inimicórum nostrórum liberáti, * serviámus illi.
verses.eng: That being delivered from the hand of our enemies, * we may serve Him without fear.

verses.lat: In sanctitáte et justítia coram ipso, * ómnibus diébus nostris.
verses.eng: In holiness and justice before Him, * all our days.

verses.lat: Et tu, puer, Prophéta Altíssimi vocáberis: * præíbis enim ante fáciem Dómini, paráre vias ejus:
verses.eng: And thou, child, shalt be called the prophet of the Highest: * for thou shalt go before the face of the Lord to prepare His ways.

verses.lat: Ad dandam sciéntiam salútis plebi ejus, * in remissiónem peccatórum eórum:
verses.eng: To give knowledge of salvation to His people, * unto the remission of their sins:

verses.lat: Per víscera misericórdiæ Dei nostri, * in quibus visitávit nos, óriens ex alto:
verses.eng: Through the bowels of the mercy of our God, * in which the Orient from on high hath visited us:

verses.lat: Illumináre his, qui in ténebris et in umbra mortis sedent: * ad dirigéndos pedes nostros in viam pacis.
verses.eng: To enlighten them that sit in darkness, and in the shadow of death: * to direct our feet into the way of peace.

verses.lat: Réquiem ætérnam * dona eis, Dómine.
verses.eng: Eternal rest * grant unto them, O Lord.

verses.lat: Et lux perpétua * lúceat eis.
verses.eng: And let perpetual light * shine upon them.

parts.label: Antiphon ad Benedíctus (repeated)
parts.lat: Ego sum * resurréctio et vita: qui credit in me, étiam si mórtuus fúerit, vivet; et omnis qui vivit et credit in me, non moriétur in ætérnum.
parts.eng: I am the resurrection and the life: * he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live; and whosoever liveth and believeth in me shall never die.

parts.label: Kýrie
parts.lat: Kýrie, eléison. Christe, eléison. Kýrie, eléison.
parts.eng: Lord, have mercy. Christ, have mercy. Lord, have mercy.

parts.label: Pater Noster (silently to ‘Et ne nos’)
parts.lat: Pater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum. Advéniat regnum tuum. Fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum quotidiánum da nobis hódie, et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris. Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem, sed líbera nos a malo. Amen.
parts.eng: Our Father, who art in heaven, hallowed be Thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth, as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread, and forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us. And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil. Amen.
parts.rubric: Said silently to ‘Et ne nos inducas’.

parts.label: Versicle
parts.lat: Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem.
parts.eng: And lead us not into temptation.

verses.lat: De profúndis clamávi ad te, Dómine: * Dómine, exáudi vocem meam:
verses.eng: Out of the depths I have cried to Thee, O Lord: * Lord, hear my voice.

verses.lat: Fiant aures tuæ intendéntes, * in vocem deprecatiónis meæ.
verses.eng: Let Thine ears be attentive * to the voice of my supplication.

verses.lat: Si iniquitátes observáveris, Dómine: * Dómine, quis sustinébit?
verses.eng: If Thou, O Lord, wilt mark iniquities: * Lord, who shall stand it?

verses.lat: Quia apud te propitiátio est: * et propter legem tuam sustínui te, Dómine.
verses.eng: For with Thee there is merciful forgiveness: * and by reason of Thy law, I have waited for Thee, O Lord.

verses.lat: Sustínuit ánima mea in verbo ejus: * sperávit ánima mea in Dómino.
verses.eng: My soul hath relied on His word: * my soul hath hoped in the Lord.

verses.lat: A custódia matutína usque ad noctem: * speret Israël in Dómino.
verses.eng: From the morning watch even until night, * let Israel hope in the Lord.

verses.lat: Quia apud Dóminum misericórdia: * et copiósa apud eum redémptio.
verses.eng: Because with the Lord there is mercy: * and with Him plentiful redemption.

verses.lat: Et ipse rédimet Israël, * ex ómnibus iniquitátibus ejus.
verses.eng: And He shall redeem Israel * from all his iniquities.

verses.lat: Réquiem ætérnam * dona eis, Dómine.
verses.eng: Eternal rest * grant unto them, O Lord.

verses.lat: Et lux perpétua * lúceat eis.
verses.eng: And let perpetual light * shine upon them.

parts.label: Versicle
parts.lat: A porta ínferi.
parts.eng: From the gates of hell.

parts.label: Versicle
parts.lat: Requiéscant in pace.
parts.eng: May they rest in peace.

parts.label: Versicle
parts.lat: Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
parts.eng: O Lord, hear my prayer.
parts.latR: Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
parts.engR: And let my cry come unto Thee.

parts.label: Versicle
parts.lat: Dóminus vobíscum.
parts.eng: The Lord be with you.

parts.label: Collect; Fidélium, Deus
parts.lat: Orémus. Fidélium, Deus, ómnium Cónditor et Redémptor, animábus famulórum famularúmque tuárum remissiónem cunctórum tríbue peccatórum: ut indulgéntiam, quam semper optavérunt, piis supplicatiónibus consequántur: Qui vivis et regnas cum Deo Patre in unitáte Spíritus Sancti Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
parts.eng: Let us pray.
